title: Pectins, 21 CFR 184.1588: direct food substances affirmed as generally recognized as safe
journal: Code of Federal Regulations, title 21, volume 3, section 184.1588, annual edition of 1 April 2025
funder: US Food and Drug Administration; the text is federal regulation published by the Office of the Federal Register.
result: The pectins (CAS 9000-69-5) are complex, high molecular weight polysaccharides found in plants and composed chiefly of partially methylated polygalacturonic acid units; the section covers high-ester pectins, low-ester pectins, amidated pectins, pectinic acids and pectinates, produced commercially by extracting citrus peel, apple pomace or beet pulp with hot dilute acid (pH 1.0 to 3.5, 70 to 90 °C) and precipitating with ethanol or isopropanol or as the copper or aluminium salt. The ingredients meet the Food Chemicals Codex, 3rd edition (1981), and are used in food with no limitation other than current good manufacturing practice, as emulsifiers and as stabilizers and thickeners. Source: 48 FR 51149, 7 November 1983. The eCFR version history lists 22 November 2016 as the latest amendment date of the section, as of 20 October 2026.
